name: Plasticity & Strengthening Mechanisms
summary: Connects dislocation behaviour to macroscopic yielding and explains every major way to make metals stronger.

topics.name: Theoretical shear strength and why real crystals are weaker
Resolved shear stress and Schmid's law; critical resolved shear stress
Single-crystal deformation: easy glide, multiple slip and stage I-III hardening
Polycrystal plasticity: Taylor factor and compatibility
Dislocation multiplication (Frank-Read sources) and forest hardening (Taylor equation)

sub.name: Precipitation and dispersion strengthening (cutting vs Orowan looping)

topics.name: Yield-point phenomena, strain ageing and Lüders bands
Temperature and strain-rate dependence of flow stress; thermally activated glide; Peierls stress in BCC
Yield criteria: Tresca and von Mises; flow rules and plastic anisotropy (Hill)
Strength-ductility trade-off and strategies to overcome it (TRIP, TWIP, bimodal grains)
Introduction to crystal plasticity and dislocation dynamics modelling
